report.summary: Reviewed perfile.py chunk 1: defines FileAnalysis dataclass, analyze_file function, and ANALYSIS_VERSION constant with extensive docstring claims. Claims about external functions/memoization/parallelism are uncheckable; internal consistency checks pass.
risks: ANALYSIS_VERSION | medium | Version bump history in docstring references '5' but no code change visible in chunk; claim that '5' added type_facts field is verifiable but the field is present; however, the docstring claims about '4' rows raising KeyError are uncheckable.

python_units_imports_and_types | high | Claim that function returns three values (units, py_imports, type_facts) but only two are used in the Python branch; third is overwritten. This is a potential bug if the function signature doesn't match.
type_facts default value | medium | Docstring claims PyTypeFacts() is safe as default and across process boundary, but this is uncheckable as PyTypeFacts definition is not in this chunk.
analyze_file purity | medium | Claim of pure function (no I/O, no globals) is uncheckable because dependencies like count_tokens, file_metrics, extract_units may have side effects.
todos: Verify that python_units_imports_and_types indeed returns three values and that the assignment to type_facts overwrites the initial default correctly.
Confirm that count_tokens, file_metrics, extract_units, imports_mod.extract_imports are pure functions with no side effects.
Check that PyTypeFacts is picklable and hashable for process boundary safety.
Ensure that the docstring claim about '4' rows raising KeyError is accurate by reviewing the _decode function in index module.

handoff.purpose: Define FileAnalysis dataclass and analyze_file function for per-file index build, with versioning and docstring claims.

symbols.name: ANALYSIS_VERSION
symbols.note: String '5'. Used as part of disk-cache key. Version history in docstring explains bumps from '3' to '5'.

symbols.name: FileAnalysis
symbols.note: Dataclass with fields: rel, lang, n_chars, n_tokens, loc, metrics, units, runs, py_imports, raw_imports, type_facts. All plain data. type_facts default is PyTypeFacts().

symbols.name: analyze_file
symbols.note: Takes rel, text, spec, ts_on. Returns FileAnalysis. Pure function (claimed). Calls python_units_imports_and_types for Python, else extract_units and imports_mod.extract_imports. Computes metrics via file_metrics, token count via count_tokens. Returns FileAnalysis with computed fields.

claims.text: Bump whenever the MEANING of any field below changes (new metric, different unit extraction, changed window hashing). It is part of the disk-cache key, so bumping it invalidates every cached entry.
claims.why: The claim about disk-cache key and invalidation refers to external caching logic not present in this chunk.

claims.text: A stale cache reporting wrong code health is far worse than a slow scan -- when in doubt, bump.
claims.why: This is a design principle, not checkable against code.

claims.text: "3": added n_tokens. A row cached under "2" has no token count, and an index built from such rows would report a denominator of zero for part of the repo -- i.e. an inflated distillation headline, silently. Bumping makes that unrepresentable.
claims.why: Refers to behavior of version '2' rows and index building, which are outside this chunk.

claims.text: "4": ``parse.py`` gained the type/field/signature extractor (``PyTypeFacts``). The digest of parse.py is already part of every key, so this bump is belt to that braces -- but the two locks fail differently and only one of them is under our control. The digest catches an EDIT to the extractor; this constant is what a reader greps for to answer "which generation of rows is in this cache", and the convention above says to bump when the meaning of a row changes. It does: a row now describes a file that has type facts, even in the generation where ``FileAnalysis`` does not yet carry them.
claims.why: Refers to parse.py and caching logic outside this chunk. The claim about FileAnalysis not carrying type_facts in version '4' is consistent with the current code having the field, but the historical state is uncheckable.

claims.text: "5": ``FileAnalysis`` now actually CARRIES them (``type_facts``). "4" rows were written by the generation that had the extractor but not the field, so they have no ``type_facts`` key at all. Those rows would decode (``_decode`` reads by subscript, so in fact they raise KeyError and become a miss) -- but relying on a KeyError being raised and swallowed is an accidental lock, not a stated one, and ``_SCHEMA`` was bumped to 2 in the same commit so they are DELETEd on open anyway. This constant is the one a reader greps to answer "which generation of rows is in this cache", and the answer changed.
claims.why: Refers to _decode function and _SCHEMA constant in external index module. The claim about KeyError is not verifiable here.

claims.text: Real tokenizer count of the file's text (tiktoken cl100k_base when installed, else tokens.count_tokens' chars/4 fallback). Carried per-file rather than recomputed at report time so it rides the disk cache: the distill ratio's DENOMINATOR then comes from the same tokenizer as its numerator, instead of a chars/4 guess. Computed in the pass that already holds the text, so it costs one encode per cache miss.
claims.why: Refers to tokenizer implementation and caching behavior outside this chunk.

claims.text: EXTRACTED UNCONDITIONALLY, even when the layer is switched off. The gate is in ``index.build_index`` (resolution + publication) and deliberately NOT here: this dataclass rides a CONTENT-KEYED disk cache, so a gate on this side would let a row written with the layer off (empty facts) be served as a HIT to a later build with the layer on -- an empty type block with no error, no exception and no log line, which is the exact silent failure the plan's Cache-Kopplung note describes. Making it unconditional costs one more walk of a tree that is already parsed (~3ms/file, and only on a cache MISS) and makes the cache correct by construction instead of by a correctly-composed key.
claims.why: Refers to index.build_index and caching strategy outside this chunk. The claim about cost (~3ms/file) is unverifiable.

claims.text: A frozen dataclass with only tuple fields is hashable and immutable, so it is safe as a PLAIN default (no default_factory) and safe to ship across a process boundary.
claims.why: Refers to PyTypeFacts definition and pickling behavior outside this chunk. The claim about safety across process boundary is not testable here.

claims.text: Pure: same inputs -> same outputs, no I/O, no globals.
claims.why: The function calls external functions (count_tokens, file_metrics, extract_units, imports_mod.extract_imports, python_units_imports_and_types) whose purity is not verifiable in this chunk.

claims.text: ONE ast.parse feeds units, imports AND type facts (it used to be two walks of one parse; it is now three walks of the same one). The units and the import records are produced by the SAME functions as before -- ``python_units_imports_and_types`` adds a third walk, it does not change the first two (invariant I1).
claims.why: Refers to python_units_imports_and_types function and its internal behavior, which is not in this chunk.

observations.what: In analyze_file, the Python branch assigns type_facts from python_units_imports_and_types, but the initial assignment type_facts = PyTypeFacts(module=rel) is overwritten. This is intentional but could be confusing.
The docstring claims about version history and caching are extensive but none are verifiable within this chunk; they reference external modules and behaviors.
The chunk ends mid-function; the return statement is missing.
observations.where: End of chunk at line ~78, after 'return FileAnalysis('
